newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks open lower, rate hike fears persist.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks open lower, rate hike fears persist.

* Toronto stocks opened lower on Thursday as investors remained skittish ahead of a possible rate hike in the U.S. * 13.1 million shares traded worth C$179.6 million.
Toronto stocks opened lower on Thursday as investors' fears of a U.S. rate hike resurfaced after a slightly higher-than-expected rise in the U.S. core April CPI data.
"They're still worried about rates next week, in spite of the fact that most people think they won't move. I mean, who knows for sure," one trader said.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index slipped 8.25 points to 6239.93 in turnover of 13.1 million shares worth C$179.6 million. Declines edged out advances 262 to 255, while 211 issues were flat.
Seven of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes were lower, led by real estate, transportation and golds.
Merchandising and metals led seven sectors higher.

U.S. treasuries extended their slump after U.S. April consumer prices rose 0.1 percent as expected, but core items rose 0.3 percent in the month. Economists had predicted a 0.2-percent increase in the core data.
Canada's unadjusted April consumer price index was flat in the month and rose 1.7 percent in the year to 137.6, Statistics Canada said on Thursday.

A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the unadjusted CPI to rise 0.2 percent on the month. The survey also forecast a 1.9 percent year-over-year rise in the all-items and 1.8 percent rise in the core CPI.
The core CPI rise of 1.8 percent was well within the Bank of Canada's target range of one to three percent.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Shares in Gandalf Technologies Inc tumbled almost 30 percent in early trade after the networking firm reported on Wednesday what President Richard Busto called disappointing fourth-quarter results. Gandalf fell 0.64 to 1.80 in active trading of more than 870,000 shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange. It was down 9/16 to 1-1/4 on Nasdaq.
